manifest.prompt: a button with custom bezier curve hover state animations that makes it feel dreamlike and ethereal, but practical for a website
consumers: design review of a rendered button
how_to_read: 1. Read the head first: the first 34 lines hold manifest, essence and routing (Read limit=34, or jq '{manifest, essence, routing}' dreamlike-button.metadump.json).
2. Pick the route for your job and run its jq: jq '<routing[i].jq>' dreamlike-button.metadump.json
3. Also pull the anti-keywords and review prompts (checks) for your scope: jq '.anti_keywords, .checks' dreamlike-button.metadump.json
4. Look up any term (lowercase): jq '.index["<term>"]' dreamlike-button.metadump.json  -> hits give id + path; not_meant lists senses to avoid.
5. Grep works too: every entry is one line, so grep -n '<word>' dreamlike-button.metadump.json returns whole entries.

essence.one_sentence: What makes a hovered button read as dreamlike is that its light and its motion arrive at different moments, so the surface seems to still be waking up after the pointer has moved on; drift, bloom, float and shimmer are four ways of staging that delay.
essence.summary: Light that spreads past the edge, a surface with no hard shadow at rest, transform and opacity that ease and linger, and a practical floor of focus, touch, reduced motion and label legibility.

formula.essential: a still surface, light revealed on its own layer, and a motion that arrives after the pointer does

roles.surface: the body the light sits on
roles.glow layer: light that rises without a hard edge
roles.curve per property: keeps arrival, glow and release apart

css-implementation.text: Material for the stylesheet, as options. Curves: drift cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) (mo-curve-drift, cv-long-tail-bloom); bloom cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1) (mo-curve-bloom); standard cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) for the lift (mo-properties); leave cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.6, 1) (mo-enter-leave); a calmer option is cv-soft-settle. Properties: transform carries the lift; opacity carries the glow, revealed from a pre-rendered layer (glow-layer); the fill can change colour (look-hover-lift-fill). Dials: lift 1 to 4 px; enter 250 to 400 ms; leave 150 to 200 ms; hover glow reveal 150 to 250 ms, with the 500 ms source reveal as one option for a slow bloom. Focus: the same glow reveal on :focus-visible, and a ring 2 to 3 px wide at a 2 to 4 px offset (opt-focus-ring). Press: a 0 to 2 px sink over 80 to 150 ms (opt-press). Touch: hover rules can sit inside @media (hover: hover) (pr-touch-no-hover). Reduced motion: the lift and the drift can reset while the colour change stays; a glow fade by opacity may stay (pr-reduced-motion). A sweep that repaints each frame is an option with a cost, not the default (ak-sweep-repaint).
css-implementation.notes: Each curve is one reading of the feel; the choice of which property takes which curve is open (opt-curve-scope).

design-review.question: Read the rendered button against the checks: does the motion keep settling without a snap, does anything move at rest, does the label read at the brightest glow frame, does keyboard focus carry the same glow?
design-review.returns: For each check: held, not held, or not tested, with its check id and the entry it came from.

ak-hover-only-feedback.instead: the same glow reveal on focus-visible, and a pressed style on touch

ak-button-physical.excluded_sense: physical push button, switch or keycap
ak-button-physical.instead: clickable web UI control with rest, hover, focus and pressed states

ak-bezier-svg.excluded_sense: SVG path or drawn Bezier shape
ak-bezier-svg.instead: cubic-bezier() timing function on CSS transition or animation properties

ak-hover-touch.excluded_sense: a touch tap, which fires no pointer-over state
ak-hover-touch.instead: pointer-over on mouse and pen; touch gets a pressed response and brief tap feedback

ak-generic-bounce.instead: a soft settle with an ease-out tail, or a small lift that lingers and comes to rest

ak-neon-glow.instead: a pale luminous haze behind the label, or a warm inner light that spreads slowly

ak-rainbow-gradient.instead: one hue family shifting a few degrees, or a faint pale sheen that crosses the face once

ak-all-at-once.instead: the surface and the label on separate timings, or the label still while the glow moves

ak-transition-all.instead: list the animated properties by name, and keep layout properties out of that list

ak-motion-at-rest.instead: motion only on hover, focus or press, one pass, then the rest state is still

ak-one-ease.instead: a curve per property, or one chosen on purpose for all (opt-curve-scope)

ak-ignore-reduced-motion.instead: keep the colour change; reset lift, drift and sweep under reduce; a glow fade by opacity may stay (opt-reduce-glow-fade)

ak-sweep-repaint.instead: animate on hover and focus with transform and opacity; a repainting sweep is one option (opt-glow-method)

k-feel-lingering.text: Does the hover motion keep easing for a while after the pointer arrives, then stop without a snap?

test.spec: Play the hover back slowly; position and glow still move past 250 ms and end without a jump.

k-response-band.text: Does the hover feedback finish inside the 150 to 400 ms band?

test.spec: Read transition-duration plus transition-delay on each hover property; the longest sits at or under 400 ms, or it is the slow bloom option.

k-composite-only.text: Do the properties that change on hover stay on transform and opacity?

k-rest-still.text: Does anything still animate on the resting button after pointer and focus leave?

test.spec: No animation or infinite keyframes on the base .btn selector; animation sits only under :hover, :focus-visible and :active.

k-reduced-motion.text: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, do the lift and the sweep stop while the colour change stays?

test.spec: A prefers-reduced-motion block resets transform and removes the animation; a colour change stays outside the reset.

k-hover-gated.text: Are the hover rules inside a hover-capable query, so a tap leaves no hover style behind?

test.spec: :hover rules sit inside @media (hover: hover) or an equivalent query.

k-focus-parity.text: Does keyboard focus show the same visible glow and lift as hover?

test.spec: Tab to the button in a browser; the glow reveal and the lift appear as on hover, and a focus ring is visible.

k-target-size.text: Is the pointer target at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels?

test.spec: getBoundingClientRect of the button is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels at its rendered size.

k-one-hue.text: Does the glow stay one pale hue, without a multi-colour gradient or a neon edge?

test.spec: Sample the glow rim; one hue family, no more than two gradient stops, low saturation at the outer edge.

k-named-transitions.text: Are the transitioned properties listed by name rather than with all?

test.spec: grep for transition:\s*all in the stylesheet returns zero matches.

k-glow-blur-fixed.text: Does the glow keep the same blur radius during hover, with only its opacity changing?

test.spec: The hover rule for the glow pseudo-element sets opacity and no filter or blur value.

k-label-contrast.text: Does the label still read clearly at the brightest glow frame?

test.spec: Contrast ratio of the label colour against the fill at the brightest glow frame; record the ratio and the threshold chosen.

q-palette.text: Which brand hue or base color does the button use?
q-palette.default: a neutral base with one soft accent hue
q-palette.resolve: ask the user or read the site's tokens

q-framework.text: Plain CSS, or a framework and component library?
q-framework.default: plain CSS with custom properties, no JavaScript

prompt._about: The user's prompt, split into clauses. Notes for the lexicon ticket: 'button' could be a physical push button; 'custom bezier curve' could be an SVG path; 'dreamlike' and 'ethereal' and 'practical' are quality words with several readings.

p-object.text: The thing being made is a button.

p-hover.text: The button has animations in its hover state.

p-bezier.text: The animations follow custom bezier curves.

p-feel.text: The button should feel dreamlike and ethereal.

p-practical.text: The result is practical for a website.

primer._about: Discipline primer for UI and interaction design, motion design for UI, and web accessibility and performance, applied to a button's hover and focus feedback. Researched facts are quoted; the rest is the builder's inference.

prim-doherty-400ms.text: Feedback should land within about 400 ms, so the user never waits on the computer.
behaviors: A hover tint that appears within 400 ms reads as immediate; a later one reads as lag
prim-doherty-400ms.principle: Flow holds when the system answers before the user has to wait.
signals: hover color settles before the pointer stops moving

prim-easing-intent.text: Material uses a standard curve for elements that move and resize, and a sharp curve for exits.
behaviors: A button's hover and press use the standard curve; an exiting tooltip or panel uses the sharp curve
An element that leaves and may come straight back should not decelerate to a stop
prim-easing-intent.principle: The curve tells the eye whether something is arriving, leaving or responding in place.
signals: a leaving element that lingers at the end of its path

prim-wcag-2-3-3.text: Motion started by an interaction must be switchable off unless it is essential to the function or information.
behaviors: A hover glow drift on a button is decorative, so it must stop when the user turns motion off
prim-wcag-2-3-3.principle: Users are not harmed or distracted by motion they did not ask for.
signals: hover animation with no reduced-motion path

prim-reduced-motion.text: The media feature reports a device setting that asks for less non-essential motion.
behaviors: Ship the drift and glow in the default rules and remove or shorten them inside the reduce block, keeping the color change
Scripted motion can check the same preference with matchMedia
prim-reduced-motion.principle: The default styles carry the motion; the reduce block takes it away.

prim-target-size.text: Pointer targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, with listed exceptions such as adequate spacing.
behaviors: A small icon button gets padding so its hit area reaches 24 by 24 CSS pixels without changing the drawn size
prim-target-size.principle: Size counts the clickable area, not only the drawn graphic.
signals: hit area smaller than 24 CSS pixels on any side

prim-mistakes.text: Looping at rest, long durations on small controls, hover-only feedback, and animated glow via box-shadow.
properties: long hover on a small control
behaviors: A looping shimmer on an idle button competes with the label and never stops
Hover-only feedback gives keyboard and touch users no response
Animating box-shadow or filter for a glow repaints each frame, unlike transform and opacity
prim-mistakes.principle: Motion should answer an action, not decorate the resting state.
signals: animation running with no pointer, focus or press

prim-duration-ranges.text: Desktop animations sit around 150 to 200 ms; past 400 ms transitions start to feel slow.
behaviors: A hover on a small control should finish well inside the 150 to 200 ms band; longer holds feel sluggish
Hover feedback of 150 to 250 ms can carry a transform and a shadow change together; under 100 ms reads as instant
prim-duration-ranges.principle: Small controls answer in the time it takes to notice the pointer.
signals: hover still moving after half a second

motion._about: Hover, focus-visible and press motion for one button. Curves and durations are dials to tune by eye, not a finished set; sourced values come from the research shards.

rs-curves-named.text: A shipping design system pairs a standard curve for hovers and entrances with an emphasized curve for page-level reveals.
behaviors: Both curves leave the start slowly, so the first frames read as a lift rather than a snap
The emphasized curve gives a longer, softer arrival than the standard one
rs-curves-named.principle: Pick the curve by intent: hovers take the standard curve, large reveals take the emphasized one.
signals: hover uses the standard curve
reveal uses the emphasized curve

cv-slow-start.text: Named ease-in curves that begin slowly and speed up, for motion that gathers before it travels.
behaviors: A y1 of 0 begins the move with zero velocity
The end of an ease-in arrives fast, so it reads as leaving rather than settling
cv-slow-start.principle: Starting slow reads as a lean into the move; it suits leaving or gathering, less so quick responses.
signals: slow first third of the motion
abrupt arrival

cv-soft-settle.text: Gentle ease-out curves that slow down steadily into rest, the mildest settle in the set.
behaviors: Every y value in this pool stays between 0 and 1, so the motion never passes its target
Lower y1 gives a slower start; the approach stays even through the middle
cv-soft-settle.principle: A settle that stays under the target reads calm and unhurried.
signals: no overshoot
even slowdown across the whole move

cv-long-tail-bloom.text: Sharp ease-out curves that cover most of the distance early, then drift the last stretch slowly.
behaviors: Most of the distance is covered in the first half, so the element seems to arrive and then linger
A y1 near 0 with a y2 of 1.000 makes the tail longest
cv-long-tail-bloom.principle: A fast arrival followed by a long, slow tail reads as a soft bloom into place.
signals: early burst of movement
visible drift at the end

cv-overshoot-lift.text: Back curves whose control points leave the 0 to 1 range, so the motion pulls back or passes its target before settling.
behaviors: A y2 above 1 carries the move past its target before it returns
A negative y1 pulls the element back before it moves forward
A small overshoot reads as a light float; a large one reads as a bounce, against a calm feel
cv-overshoot-lift.principle: A brief overshoot reads as lift or give; dial it down at button scale.
signals: a y value outside 0 to 1
a visible pass beyond the end position

cv-in-out-drift.text: Ease-in-out curves that start and end gently; mirrored control points ease out at the rate they eased in.
behaviors: Mirrored control points give a move that eases out at the same rate it eased in
Sine and quad keep the middle even, so the move does not snap through the centre
cv-in-out-drift.principle: Gentle in-out curves keep the middle even; the steep ones are a separate reading.
signals: flat ends
even middle

cv-in-out-steep.text: Steep in-out curves concentrate the move into a short middle, with flat ends that read as a step.
behaviors: The steeper the middle, the more the move snaps through the centre
ease_in_out_expo has a near-instant middle with flat ends, so it reads as a step rather than a drift
cv-in-out-steep.principle: Steep middles suit a quick state change more than a slow, lingering feel.
signals: flat ends
fast middle section

ap-layout-paint-costly.term: properties that trigger layout or paint
ap-layout-paint-costly.text: Animating width or height changes the page geometry, which forces layout; the layout is usually followed by a repaint that costs more again.
behaviors: Animating width moves or resizes neighbouring elements
Layout cost is typically dwarfed by the repaint that follows it
ap-layout-paint-costly.principle: A change that drags other elements along costs more than the change itself.
signals: width or height in an animation
neighbouring elements shifting during motion

ap-thread-split.text: Styling, layout, paint and JavaScript run on the main thread; compositor-only animation does not wait for it.
behaviors: Paint or layout inside an animation puts the work back on the main thread, for CSS and JavaScript alike
A busy page interrupts main-thread animation, not compositor animation
ap-thread-split.principle: Where an animation runs decides whether a busy page can stall it.

ap-will-change.text: will-change tells the browser ahead of time which properties will change, so it can prepare; the guide warns that overuse wastes resources.
behaviors: Declared for transform and opacity, it lets the browser prepare optimizations before the change starts
Applied to every element in view it can cost more than it saves
ap-will-change.principle: Declare the hint only when the animation is about to start, not for the whole page.
signals: will-change on elements that do not animate
will-change on many elements at once

mo-curve-bloom.text: For the soft bloom reading, a steady ease-out quart that brightens the glow without overshoot.
behaviors: Glow opacity follows this curve so brightening finishes with the lift
mo-curve-bloom.principle: A bloom should arrive evenly; a sharp curve on glow reads as a flash.

tokens.duration_ms_dial: 250 to 500; shorter stays crisp, longer reads as haze

mo-curve-float.text: For the gentle float reading, a curve with a y2 just above 1 so the lift overshoots a little and settles.
behaviors: A y2 near 1.0 gives no float; near 1.08 gives a small one; past about 1.2 reads as a bounce, against a calm feel
mo-curve-float.principle: Overshoot is a float at the end of the move; keep it small.

mo-curve-drift.text: For a lingering reading, several curves can carry it: a long-tail ease-out, a soft ease-out quart for glow, or a standard curve with a slow arrival. Each is one reading of the feel.
behaviors: An early burst answers the pointer; the tail carries the lingering feel
A tail past about 500 ms reads as lag rather than drift
mo-curve-drift.principle: Where a curve puts its tail decides which reading it gives: early for response, late for drift.

tokens.duration_ms_dial: 250 to 400, inside the researched band; a longer tail is opt-drift-long-tail

mo-enter-leave.text: Enter takes the chosen curve inside the researched band; leave is shorter and steeper so the release does not linger.
behaviors: A CSS transition retargets from the current value when the pointer leaves mid-move, so the button returns without a jump
Keyframe animations do not retarget, so a pointer that leaves early waits for the loop to finish
mo-enter-leave.principle: Arrival is savored; departure gets out of the way.
signals: leave ends before the pointer reaches the next control

mo-properties.text: transform carries the lift, opacity carries the glow, and the glow is a pre-rendered sibling layer. Fixed blur and shadow are the constraint; a bloom that grows with the lift is opt-glow-bloom.
behaviors: transform on the standard curve cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) keeps the lift crisp
A glow delay of 0 to 80 ms behind the lift reads as a follow-through; past about 100 ms it reads as late
mo-properties.principle: Only compositor properties change during the move, so the frame cost stays low.

ap-composite-cheap.text: Transform and opacity are the cheap properties to animate; the browser can highly optimize both, whether JavaScript or CSS drives them.
behaviors: Animating transform or opacity avoids layout and paint on the main thread
The same motion runs on the compositor thread and keeps going while the main thread is busy
The article calls transform and opacity the only two compositor-only properties; check that against current browsers before relying on it
ap-composite-cheap.principle: Frame cost is set by which properties change, and by how many layers exist.
signals: only transform and opacity in the keyframes
no width, height or geometry in the animation

mo-dreamlike.text: Motion that seems to drift rather than snap: slow, soft and a little unreal. It reads as one of four motions, and no reading is the default.

readings.in_practice: position eases in with a long tail, so the button seems to settle after it arrives
signals: motion still moving after 250 ms
stops softly with no snap

readings.in_practice: glow opacity and spread rise with the lift, brightening over the label
signals: glow brightens, no hard edge
light thins toward the outside

readings.in_practice: a small upward lift that passes its rest point by a few pixels and returns
signals: button passes rest by 1 to 3 px, then returns

readings.in_practice: one soft light pass across the face on hover, focus or press
signals: one pass, then still
no motion at rest

glow-sweep.text: A keyframe moves background-position from 0% to 400% over the cycle, so each gradient color crosses the button in turn.
behaviors: Each color enters from the side and leaves on the other side, one after another
Because the sweep is linear, the speed stays even across the cycle
glow-sweep.principle: The gradient is wider than the button, so moving its position is what reads as light moving.
signals: background-position in keyframes
linear and infinite on one animation

look._about: Surface and light of the button: the ethereal quality word, the rest and hover looks, and what a glow costs. Dials are illustrative ranges, not measured values.

options._about: options, not requirements: cheaper or different ways to get a similar glow, each with its cost

opt-glow-radial.text: A radial gradient on the glow layer that fades to transparent gives a haze with no filter at all.
behaviors: The gradient falloff does the softening that a blur would do
Without a blur pass the halo costs less to draw, but a hard stop shows as a ring

tokens.fade_end_pct: 50 to 70: where the gradient reaches transparent; larger spreads the haze wider

opt-glow-small-blur.text: Use a smaller blur radius on small buttons, where the blurred area is a bigger share of the element.

tokens.blur_px: 8 to 16 on buttons under about 200px wide

look-rest-surface.text: At rest the button is a quiet, partly see-through surface with a faint edge light, so hover has room to brighten.
behaviors: A translucent fill lets the page colour through, which reads as light rather than paint
A fill near full opacity hides the glow behind it, so the glow shows only at the edges
look-rest-surface.principle: Rest sets the floor; hover is measured against it, so the rest state stays quiet.
signals: fill alpha between 0.6 and 0.9
highlight line along the top edge

tokens.surface_alpha: 0.6 to 0.9: lower lets more page through and reads airier; near 1 reads solid
tokens.edge_light_px: 1: thicker reads as a border rather than light

look-hover-lift-fill.term: hover state: luminosity, lift and pale fill
look-hover-lift-fill.text: On hover the fill brightens, the button rises slightly and the glow fades in; each change is a separate property with its own curve.
behaviors: Lift moves transform, which the compositor can run without repainting the label
Mixing the fill toward white keeps its hue, so the change reads as light rather than a new colour
look-hover-lift-fill.principle: Hover adds light and height in small steps; no single property carries the whole effect.
signals: transform in the hover rule
lightness change without a hue change

tokens.lift_px: 1 to 4: past 4 the button reads as jumping; under 1 it is hard to see
tokens.fill_mix_white_pct: 8 to 18: more brightens and can wash the label out

look-soft-shadow.text: A wide, low-alpha shadow under the button that reads as height rather than as a hard edge.
behaviors: A larger blur at a lower alpha reads as more distance from the page
A shadow whose size changes on hover repaints every frame, so keeping its size fixed and moving the element is cheaper
look-soft-shadow.principle: Height comes from the shadow's softness and the element's offset together.
signals: blur 16 to 32px
alpha 0.1 to 0.2
shadow size identical at rest and hover

tokens.shadow_blur_px: 16 to 32: wider is softer and more floating; narrower reads as a card edge
tokens.shadow_alpha: 0.1 to 0.2: higher reads as a hard drop shadow

look-label-contrast.text: The label keeps a contrast floor against the fill at the glow's brightest frame. 4.5:1 is the usual text target; the WCAG value was not fetched in this build.

tokens.check: measure label against fill at the brightest glow frame

look-ethereal.text: Ethereal light has no hard source or edge: a glow, a haze, or a lift without a heavy shadow. It has four readings, each with its own light source.

readings.reading: a luminous glow behind the label
readings.in_practice: light rises from behind the text: a soft halo brightens the label area on hover
signals: halo brighter than the fill

readings.reading: a translucent haze that thins toward the edges
readings.in_practice: the fill is denser at the centre, so the page shows through near the rim
signals: fill alpha below 0.9

readings.reading: a weightless lift with a soft, spread shadow
readings.in_practice: the button rises a few pixels over a wide, faint shadow with no hard edge
signals: lift under 4px, wide blur at low alpha

readings.reading: a pale, airy fill that lightens on hover
readings.in_practice: the rest fill is a light tint; hover lifts it toward white and the hue stays
signals: lightness up, hue unchanged

look-ethereal.principle: Ethereal is first a question of where the light comes from; the motion comes after.

look-glow-cost.term: glow or blur on hover, and its cost
look-glow-cost.text: A glow is a second layer. Its blur is the expensive part, and the cost depends on whether the blur or the shadow changes during the animation.
behaviors: Animating box-shadow or blur radius repaints the area every frame
Opacity alone on a drawn layer can move on the compositor; measure it in devtools, since browsers differ
Animating background-position repaints the button; transform or opacity does not
look-glow-cost.principle: Pay for the blur once: fix its radius and animate only what the compositor can move.
signals: filter or box-shadow in the transition list
opacity alone in the transition list

tokens.glow_blur_px: 12 to 24: wider and softer halo; large blurs cost more to draw on a big button
tokens.glow_outset_px: 4 to 8: how far the halo reaches past the edge

glow-layer.text: A ::before copy of the button sits behind it, offset 5px on each side, blurred by filter, and hidden with opacity 0 at rest.
behaviors: The glow copies the gradient through background: inherit, so its colour follows the button
Blur spreads the copy past the box, so the edge reads as light, not a border
Revealing a pre-rendered glow by opacity avoids the per-frame repaint of an animated box-shadow
Blur radius stays fixed during hover; only opacity animates
glow-layer.principle: A second, blurred layer of the same surface: render it once, reveal it, never animate a shadow.
signals: content: '' pseudo-element
only opacity changes

glow-hover-state.term: hover swap to a gradient and reveal
glow-hover-state.text: On hover the button takes a four-stop gradient at 400% background size, the glow fades to opacity 1, and the animation starts.
behaviors: The glow appears by opacity alone; its size and position do not change on hover
The text sits above the glow through z-index, not through a separate element
glow-hover-state.principle: Hover changes which layer is visible and what color it carries; the motion comes next.
signals: background-size above 100%
two z-index values flipped on hover

glow-dials.text: The page names four dials: blur radius, outset, background size and cycle length. Each changes the look in a known direction.
behaviors: A larger blur radius spreads the glow further and softens its edge; the page's 20px is a starting point
A larger background-size stretches each color across more of the button, so the sweep feels slower across the face
A shorter cycle makes the sweep faster; the page's 8s is a starting point
glow-dials.principle: Each dial trades reach, legibility of the text, and speed against each other.
signals: glow wider than the button
text edges blurred by the glow

lexicon._about: Brain-dump vocabulary for a dreamlike, ethereal, practical button. Seed material and options, not requirements. Curve values, durations and glow specifics live in the 30, 31, 32 and research shards; this section names them by id.

lx-influences._about: Lineages that bring one quality each. Named from memory, not fetched: check before citing.

contribution: soft gradations with no hard outline
deliberate blur that reads as atmosphere
light as a surface rather than an object
a glowing edge where a plane seems to float
inf-turrell.transfers: a glow that reads as a plane

contribution: easing at both ends so motion reads as gentle
timing carries feeling more than distance
animation principles from classic character animation

queries: slow ease out hover button css
cheap glow animation alternative to box-shadow

rs-ex-unless-motion.text: A deep-cut design system that names two curves and assigns each to an intent, hovers versus page reveals.
rs-ex-unless-motion.contribution: The split of one curve per intent, with the standard curve on hovers.
rs-ex-unless-motion.transfers: The intent-to-curve assignment and the naming of tokens
rs-ex-unless-motion.does_not_transfer: The brand, palette and layout of the system

lx-assoc.term: how people talk about dreamy motion
lx-assoc.text: Everyday phrases for the feel; use them as search words and as tone checks, not as specs. Deep cuts sit in lx-influences.
signals: a glow that thins toward the edges
a lift with no hard shadow

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices where nothing decides them

opt-curve-scope.term: one curve or a curve per property
opt-curve-scope.text: One curve for everything keeps the motion coherent; a drift for position and a bloom for glow separates the two feelings and costs one more token.

opt-states.term: hover only or hover, focus-visible and press
opt-states.text: Hover alone is quieter; matching motion on focus-visible and press gives keyboard and touch users the same feel, at the cost of more moving parts.

opt-press.text: A pressed style while the pointer or finger is down: the face sinks a little and the glow dims back to rest.
behaviors: A press that sinks 1 to 2 px reads as a click without a glow change
A press shorter than hover keeps the click answer quick
opt-press.principle: Press answers a click or tap at once and returns on release.

tokens.depth_px: 0 to 2 (translateY); deeper reads as a sink
tokens.curve: a short ease-out such as cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)

opt-focus-ring.text: A visible focus ring on focus-visible, drawn on top of the glow so the focus position stays findable.

tokens.colour: visible against both the fill and the page; check it at the brightest glow frame

opt-glow-bloom.term: soft bloom, spread grows with lift
opt-glow-bloom.text: Glow spread and opacity rise together with the lift, so the light widens as the button rises. Animating blur or spread repaints each frame, so it costs more (pr-performance).

opt-glow-slow-reveal.text: The source's own 500 ms glow reveal. Past the 400 ms ceiling it reads slow for hover, so keep it for a deliberate, slow bloom.

opt-drift-long-tail.text: A 400 to 800 ms settle, the long tail the lingering reading leans on. It sits past the researched 400 ms ceiling, so it is a deliberate choice for a slow drift.

opt-reduce-glow-fade.text: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the lift, drift and sweep reset, and the glow may still fade by opacity. The colour change stays either way.

opt-glow-method.term: glow by opacity or by shadow
opt-glow-method.text: A pre-rendered glow that fades by opacity is cheapest; a box-shadow drawn once on a sibling layer and faded in does the same job. An animated box-shadow or blur on a large button looks richer and repaints each frame.

practical._about: Practical use of a dreamlike hover: keyboard, touch, reduced motion, cost, legibility and rest. Sourced where a standard speaks; the rest is inferred, and choices sit in the options group.

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices where nothing decides them

opt-reduce-color-only.text: Under reduce, remove all movement and keep only the color change on hover and focus.

opt-focus-same-glow.text: Keyboard focus runs the same glow reveal as hover, at the same speed.

opt-focus-static-glow.text: Keyboard focus shows the glow at full opacity with no fade; motion stays on pointer hover only.

opt-touch-tap-bloom.text: On touch, one brief bloom plays on tap and then the button rests.

opt-reduce-short-fade.text: Under reduce, keep a 150 to 200 ms opacity fade, or shorten the drift, lift and sweep to a few tens of milliseconds.

opt-touch-press-only.text: On touch, the pressed style while the finger is down is one response; no hover is needed.

pr-focus-parity.text: Keyboard focus shows the same visible state as hover, so the motion carries over without a pointer.
behaviors: Hover-only feedback leaves keyboard users with no response, so the reveal also keys off :focus-visible
A focus ring kept on top of the glow keeps the focus position findable
pr-focus-parity.principle: Whatever a pointer sees, a keyboard user sees too, through a rule that does not depend on the pointer.
signals: hover and focus-visible share one rule
Tab to the button shows the glow

pr-touch-no-hover.text: Touch screens have no hover, and a tapped hover style can stick until the next tap, so hover rules belong inside a hover-capable query.
behaviors: Wrapping hover rules in (hover: hover) keeps a tapped button from holding its glow after the finger lifts
The pressed style is the response touch users get, and it needs no hover
pr-touch-no-hover.principle: The press is the response touch gives; a hover left on after a tap reads as a stuck state.
signals: glow still visible after a tap with no pointer
pressed style visible while the finger is down

pr-compositor-invariant.text: Holds for the cheap path. A background-position sweep breaks it on purpose, and its cost is priced in pr-performance.
pr-compositor-invariant.never_implies: A static glow that never animates is not a practical glow by itself.
pr-compositor-invariant.principle: The invariant is what keeps a hover cheap on a busy page.

pr-reduced-motion.text: Under the reduce setting, hover motion is decorative and may be switched off; the colour change stays.
properties: glow fade by opacity may survive (opt-reduce-glow-fade)
behaviors: WCAG 2.3.3 allows interaction motion to be disabled unless essential, and a glow is not essential
A reduce block that stops the sweep but keeps an opacity reveal still changes state without moving the button
pr-reduced-motion.principle: The default styles carry the motion; the reduce block decides how much of it stays.

pr-quality-practical.text: Practical, for a website control: fast feedback, settled states, usable by keyboard, touch and reduced motion. It has four readings; no reading is the default.

readings.in_practice: feedback lands within about 400 ms and settles without a wait
signals: color settles before the pointer stops
no visible lag on the first frame

readings.in_practice: focus-visible matches hover; touch gets a press response
signals: Tab shows the glow
the pressed style appears under a finger

readings.in_practice: drift and sweep are removed or shortened, and the color change stays
signals: a prefers-reduced-motion block
no infinite keyframes inside that block

readings.reading: keeps text legible and never loops at rest
readings.in_practice: label contrast holds at the glow's brightest state; nothing animates at rest
signals: glow behind the label, not over it
no infinite animation on the resting button

pr-legibility-rest.text: The glow spreads past the button and can wash over the label; the label's contrast at the glow's brightest frame is the check to run.
behaviors: A blurred glow behind the label lowers its contrast on each frame it brightens
A looping sweep on an idle button competes with the label and never stops
pr-legibility-rest.principle: Motion should answer an action, not decorate the resting state.

questions: At the glow's brightest frame, does the label still read clearly?
Does anything still animate on a button at rest, after pointer and focus leave?
If the sweep loops, should it run only while hovered or focused?

pr-performance.text: Transform and opacity run on the compositor; box-shadow, blur and background-position repaint, so a large animated blurred glow costs the most.
behaviors: A pre-rendered glow revealed by opacity keeps paint off each frame
A background-position sweep over a large face repaints it every frame
will-change declared just before hover avoids keeping layers alive at rest
pr-performance.principle: Animate only what the compositor moves, and render the glow once and reveal it.
signals: paint flashing on the button during hover
only transform and opacity in the keyframes

worn._about: Worn paths: what a lazy output of this prompt tends to produce. Options, not rules; each one names a fresher move.

worn-paths.term: worn paths for a dreamlike hover button
worn-paths.text: The first thing most builds reach for is a bouncy, neon, pulsing button with one 0.3s ease on everything.
behaviors: A bounce reads as playful, not dreamlike: the motion settles instead of rebounding
A neon glow is saturated and hard-edged; an ethereal glow is pale and diffuse
One curve for color, position and shadow makes the button feel like a single timer
A pulse that never stops draws the eye at rest and fights the label
Motion while idle gives no information about what the user did
worn-paths.principle: Worn paths come from the first default that arrives; a dreamlike button comes from a few deliberate, different choices.
signals: transition: all
one cubic-bezier for every property
box-shadow inside an infinite keyframe
saturated hue in a gradient
no prefers-reduced-motion query
bounce keyframe with overshoot
